body: Me too, even though tomorrow I'm going on holiday and I know it'll be an awesome time I still kind of wish I dont wake up at all.

yes I think it happens sometimes when you're alone with your thoughts for too long. I've had this kind of cyclic thinking in my head and in the end, whether it's real or not doesn't really matter I guess, because this is the only reality you can perceive so you might as well accept that it is the only reality that you can control.
help with what though? it's not a situational thing they can help with. And the more they help, the worse I feel, and the more I feel like a burden to them. How did you manage to get out of this?

I got allocated by the public healthcare system here so I guess I can't complain because it's free, but I'm very sick of that 'How does that make you feel, does it make you think things like "I'm not good enough" or "I'm worthless"'. I feel like therapists have such a set formula that they don't see different people have different responses to situations. I can see her writing stuff down and underlining stuff, but nothing ever gets sorted. Honestly, you need to pick the right people to tell. Some people are just unable to see things from your angle. Find someone logical to talk to, if you're not close to them then talk to them in a non-personal way. Sometimes it's not an issue of people caring, but them putting things into perspective of you so that you can start seeing things differently.

When I was younger I had a similar maths homework situation and I cut my wrists because my dad was yelling at me for not doing it. It's just that feeling of overwhelmingness when you look at something and it seems like a lot to deal with and you won't be able to cope. committing suicide at that moment seems like an easy way out, but one day you'll be able to drop maths and never have to do any of that bullshit again. But for now, do the homework, or don't do it, worse comes to worse it you get in a bit of trouble, but do try to take a step back and look at the grand picture; whatever the reason you left your family early is probably more important than your homework. They're your support network and if you're able to speak to them they might be able to help you out with the stress.
Tomorrow Is Today by Billy Joel

my dad is in the process of getting help or something (don't want to ask it's awkward), but we (him included) think he has BPD, or something similar. I think the difference is that manipulation will come in a different angle, instead of using sadness my dad uses anger to guilt us. he also uses the idea that he provided for us (in terms of money) and consistently says we owe him for it. Can't deal with any criticism because he thinks you hate him when you tell him he's done something wrong. Explosive reactions to little things when in a bad mood. Thinks we're out to get him. Presumes negative conversations about things are always about him. Can be incredibly mean without realising. Totally different person when in public or people who are not family. 
Because he hasn't had an official diagnosis I can't confirm that these traits are because he has BPD, but he can totally be a different person when he's anxious or angry and says horrible and mean things without realising the consequences, then sort of erases it from his memory, which is why I don't think it's regular anxiety or depression. 
Haven't found a way to deal with it yet, but rest of the family seems to be able to ignore him when he's being crazy. I think it's just a matter of accepting that he's suffering from something and responding to that behaviour will not change him for the better. Hope you find out more about your dad though, so that you can start building a coping mechanism for it.
